title: VIX December 2027 expiration — the OIC/OCC's PUBLISHED date, which this research finds is a seven-day publisher error; Cboe's rule and Cboe's own realized settlement history both give 2027-12-22
source: EST: THIS ENTRY TRACKS A DATE ITS OWN RESEARCH CONCLUDES IS WRONG, AND SAYS SO IN THE TITLE. It exists because the OIC/OCC publishes it and a member may meet it on a broker calendar, not because this lane believes a VIX SOQ prints on 2027-12-15. THE PUBLISHED ROW: optionseducation.org/api/expirationcalendar, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 34,871 bytes), carries 'Monthly Volatility Products Expiration date' on 2027-12-15, and the OCC's SECOND artifact — the print-ready 2027 Expiration Calendar PDF, 'accurate as of 12/18/2025', a different generation two weeks earlier, rasterized and read by eye this session — carries the identical purple mark on Wednesday the 15th. The publisher is INTERNALLY CONSISTENT and, this research finds, consistently wrong; the sibling proposal that called it internally inconsistent is corrected here. THE GOVERNING RULE, READ FROM THE PRIMARY THIS SESSION (cboe.com/tradable-products/vix/vix-futures/specifications, HTTP 200, 461,361 bytes, rule text recovered from the page's Next.js flight payload — a sibling recorded this body as unreadable and it is not): 'The final settlement date for a contract with the "VX" ticker symbol is on the Wednesday that is 30 days prior to the third Friday of the calendar month immediately following the month in which the contract expires', with settlement moving to the preceding business day 'if that Wednesday or the Friday that is 30 days following that Wednesday is a Cboe Options holiday'. January 2028's third Friday is 2028-01-21; the Wednesday 30 days prior is 2027-12-22; neither leg is a holiday, so the clause does not fire. THE FILE'S OWN ROW IS SELF-REFUTING: 2027-12-15 plus 30 days is 2028-01-14, the SECOND Friday of January 2028, which is not the standard monthly series the rule names. VALIDATION RUN IN-SESSION, NOT INHERITED: the rule plus its holiday clause reproduces the settlement date for all 217 months in 2008-07 -> 2026-09 for which Cboe's own VRO print series carries a row (the 218th, 2013-05, has no print at any date in Cboe's file), and it reproduces 35 of the OIC/OCC calendar's 36 volatility rows — the sole miss being this one. THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE IS A CALENDAR TWIN: 2010 and 2027 are the same calendar (both non-leap, both starting Friday). Cboe's realized 2010 monthly SOQ prints run 01-20, 02-17, 03-17, 04-21, 05-19, 06-16, 07-21, 08-18, 09-15, 10-20, 11-17, 12-22 — ten of twelve identical in day-of-month to the OIC's published 2027 rows, with May's one-day difference fully explained by the Juneteenth clause (a holiday that did not exist in 2010) and DECEMBER the only unexplained one: realized 2010-12-22 against published 2027-12-15. Stays estimate rather than being deleted or re-dated: the id encodes the date, this lane may not write the sibling id's canonical file, and an estimate widens caution and licenses nothing. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: SEEDED as proposals/vix-expiration-2027-12-15.from-fomc-minutes-2027-12-29.json (2026-09-08), read in full before this canonical file was written, which now shadows it. THE CALENDAR DELIBERATELY CARRIES TWO IDS FOR ONE SETTLEMENT and that is the honest state, not a bug: this id is the publisher's date, and vix-expiration-2027-12-22 (a sibling lane's proposal, untouched here) is the rule's date. They cannot both be real. This lane's call is that 2027-12-22 is the settlement and this row is an artifact; the sibling owns its own file and its own conclusion. RESOLUTION, mechanical and not a matter of argument: VX/Z7 appearing on any Cboe settlement or expiration-calendar surface. Dated 2027-12-22 -> this id is retired by whoever owns it then. Dated 2027-12-15 -> this research is wrong, the OCC is the venue's own record, and this id promotes under OCC: while the sibling retires. VX/Z7 is unlisted today (Cboe's strip stopped at VX/K7 as of 2026-09-04), so neither can be settled now. THE ERROR'S GENERATING MECHANISM, named precisely and testable out of sample: 2027-12-15 is exactly 2027-11-17 + 28 days. A naive 'previous month + four weeks' carry-forward agrees with the rule for December 2025 (+28) and December 2026 (+28) and diverges for the first time at December 2027, where the correct step is 35 days because January 2028's third Friday sits at its latest possible position (the 21st, since 2028-01-01 is a Saturday). It is the only 35-day November-to-December step in the file's span, and the December row is structurally the one row per annual calendar whose anchor month falls outside that calendar's own year. December 2028 is the next divergence (+28 gives 2028-12-13, the rule gives 2028-12-20), which is registered as a forward test. NOTHING TRADEABLE IS CLAIMED. symbols is empty, impact is low, no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is settlement-keyed, and the sibling ledgers have measured the settlement configuration inert on every channel they tested. Estimate; estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
